questions.q: What are Cascade's four Lead Source picklist values?
options: Cold Call, Email Blast, Billboard, Radio Ad
Trade Show, Website Inquiry, Referral, Partner/Dealer
Inbound, Outbound, Marketing Qualified, Sales Qualified
LinkedIn, Google Ads, Direct Mail, Walk-In
questions.explain: The lesson sets the Lead Source picklist to exactly these four values, matching the lead channels introduced in Lesson 2: Trade Show, Website Inquiry, Referral, and Partner/Dealer.

questions.q: Why does Jordan Kessler, the SDR, own every new Lead regardless of source, rather than Tom Baptiste or Priya Nair?
options: Because Kessler has the System Administrator profile
Because his job is to confirm it's a real business and qualify budget/timeline before handing off to a closing rep
Because Leads cannot be owned by Account Executives in Salesforce
Because Key Accounts only works Opportunities, never Leads
questions.explain: The lesson explains Jordan's role as SDR is to qualify every new Lead first, then convert and reassign ownership to Baptiste or Nair depending on account size -- that's why new Leads default to his queue.

questions.q: Which two fields must be set manually by the converting user rather than through the Lead conversion mapping, and why?
options: Email and Phone, because Salesforce never maps contact information automatically
Lead Source and Company, because they cannot be mapped to Opportunity
Business Segment on the new Account and Contact Role on the new Contact, because a Lead doesn't carry that distinction on its own
First Name and Last Name, because Leads do not have name fields
questions.explain: The lesson states Business Segment and Contact Role have no source field on the Lead carrying that exact distinction, so the converting rep sets them manually during conversion rather than through the automated mapping.

questions.q: What stage does a newly converted Opportunity default to?
options: Closed Won
Negotiation/Review
Equipment Proposal
Qualifying
questions.explain: The lesson states the Opportunity created during conversion defaults to the Qualifying stage -- the first stage in Cascade's five-stage sales process from Lesson 2.

questions.q: What is the first thing Salesforce does when a Lead is converted, before creating any new records?
options: It deletes the original Lead record immediately
It emails the Contact a welcome message
It checks whether the Company name matches an existing Account, to avoid creating a duplicate
It assigns the new Opportunity to Monica Reyes
questions.explain: The lesson lists this as the first step of conversion: Salesforce checks whether the Company name matches an existing Account before creating or updating any records, to avoid duplicating accounts Cascade already works with.
